about: What the generated instructions for Blender on Linux must say and must not say (Lane BL1, Orbit's Blender sidecar, and Lane BL2, its game-asset families, 2026-11-13), in the shape of Lane G's pack-inputs.json. Every fact is as built at the kernel commit named and names its evidence: a case of the real-Blender suite desktop/oshal-node/scripts/test-blender-plugin-desktop.cjs (the Spark's Blender 5.1.0 through its launcher ~/.local/bin/blender, in a private display with scratch folders, Orbit's real plugin door and install; 12 of 12) or of the game-asset suite desktop/oshal-node/scripts/test-blender-game-asset.cjs (the same Blender with the Spark's Godot 4.7.2; 8 of 8) and, where a sentence or a rule is quoted, the Orbit or add-on source it is read from. Orbit reports a bound Blender on the blender bridge with its own --version (linux-program-versions.ts, `Blender 5.1.0`, version kind file). The verbs are in blender-bridge-facts.json beside this file. `acceptance` is the check a written text is held to: `contains` are phrases it must hold, `absent` are phrases it must not.

programs.name: Blender (with Orbit's Blender add-on)

must_say.fact: A snapshot ("action": "snapshot") reads the whole open .blend through Orbit's Blender add-on: a File line (its name, whether it has unsaved changes, Blender's version, the mode), a Scene line per scene, an Object line per object (type, location, rotation in degrees, scale, mesh vertex and face counts, parent, modifiers, materials), a Material line per material (base color as #RRGGBB, metallic, roughness, who uses it) and the Selection with the active object.
must_say.evidence: scripts/test-blender-plugin-desktop.cjs case "a snapshot reads the whole file and declares the Blender actions"; desktop/oshal-node/src/main/bridges/blender.ts composeScene; desktop/oshal-node/plugins/blender/orbit_scene.py read_file

must_say.fact: Blender is never typed into, pressed or selected: every change is "action": "invoke" with a declared verb and its inputs, the object named by its name in object (the active object when none is named). Each object of a snapshot is an element with the role object and is read only.
must_say.evidence: desktop/oshal-node/src/main/bridges/blender.ts (write and editor() refuse an object; typeRefusal: "Blender's objects change through its declared actions"); scripts/test-blender-plugin-desktop.cjs case "a refused edit changes nothing and says what Blender has" (press, select and type into an object are refused in those words and the file is unchanged)

must_say.fact: Each edit is one named step on Blender's own undo list, "Jarvis: <what> (#tag)", so the person's Ctrl+Z in Blender takes it back. "action": "undo" with the change takes it back with Blender's own Undo only while it is Blender's latest step; when other changes came after it, the answer says so and nothing is undone.
must_say.evidence: scripts/test-blender-plugin-desktop.cjs cases "add-primitive is one named step that Ctrl+Z on the keyboard takes back" (Ctrl+Z pressed through XTEST) and "transform-object, set-material-color and delete-object, each taken back by Orbit's undo" (a step that is not the latest is refused: "other changes after that one"); desktop/oshal-node/plugins/blender/orbit_snippet.py push and undo

must_say.fact: Rotation is in degrees, location in Blender units, and scale is one number or [x, y, z]. transform-object with relative: true adds to the location and rotation and multiplies the scale. add-primitive makes a cube, plane, uv-sphere, ico-sphere, cylinder, cone, torus, monkey, circle or grid with UVs, at the 3D cursor unless location is given, and selects it.
must_say.evidence: scripts/test-blender-plugin-desktop.cjs case "transform-object, set-material-color and delete-object" (location [1, 2, 3], rotation [0, 0, 90], scale 2 read back as such); desktop/oshal-node/plugins/blender/orbit_verbs.py add_primitive and transform_object

must_say.fact: set-material-color takes color as "#RRGGBB", as Blender's color picker shows it, or [r, g, b] from 0 to 1, with metallic and roughness from 0 to 1; an object with no material gets a new one. The snapshot's Material line then shows the color as #RRGGBB.
must_say.evidence: scripts/test-blender-plugin-desktop.cjs (color "#FF0000", roughness 0.25 read back as "Material Crate Material: base color #FF0000, metallic 0, roughness 0.25; used by Crate"); desktop/oshal-node/plugins/blender/orbit_scene.py color

must_say.fact: An edit Blender refuses changes nothing, and its words say why: an unknown object lists the objects there are, a modifier setting Blender does not have lists the settings it has, and a parent that would make a loop is refused.
must_say.evidence: scripts/test-blender-plugin-desktop.cjs case "a refused edit changes nothing and says what Blender has" (the snapshot is the same text before and after) and the set-parent loop refusal in "modifiers, parenting, rename and a keyframe"

must_say.fact: Modifiers are named by Blender's types (SUBSURF, BEVEL, MIRROR, ARRAY, SOLIDIFY, DECIMATE, TRIANGULATE, WELD, BOOLEAN and the rest) and set by Blender's own property names, such as {"levels": 2}; apply-modifier applies one to the mesh, as a game engine needs it.
must_say.evidence: scripts/test-blender-plugin-desktop.cjs case "modifiers, parenting, rename and a keyframe for a game asset" (a subdivision of levels 2, set to 1, applied: 26 vertices, 24 faces)

must_say.fact: Blender is edited only in Object Mode: while the person is in Edit Mode or another mode, an edit is refused with words asking them to press Tab in Blender.
must_say.evidence: desktop/oshal-node/plugins/blender/orbit_serve.py edit ("Jarvis edits in Object Mode only, so press Tab in Blender and ask again"); code only

must_say.fact: export-glb writes a glTF binary .glb into folder (a path, or beside the .blend) of the whole scene, the listed objects or selectedOnly, modifiers applied, Y up. When the folder is inside a Godot project, the answer gives the res:// path Godot imports it as; that is the hand-off to Godot.
must_say.evidence: scripts/test-blender-plugin-desktop.cjs case "save-file names the file, and export-glb hands Godot a res:// path" ("Godot imports it as res://assets/barrel.glb"; the file starts with glTF)

must_say.fact: save-file saves in place; a file never saved needs as (a file name, saved beside it or in Documents). Another file of that name is replaced only with overwrite: true.
must_say.evidence: scripts/test-blender-plugin-desktop.cjs case "save-file names the file" (refused "this file was never saved: name it with as", then saved as game asset.blend)

must_say.fact: run-python follows the person's two Python switches in Blender, which the snapshot's Python snippets line states: off, it is refused; on and asking (the default), call it without confirmed, put the answer's question to the person, and call again with confirmed: true only after their yes; on without asking, it runs at once. A scheduled turn never runs Python, and a snippet stops after five seconds.
must_say.evidence: scripts/test-blender-plugin-desktop.cjs cases "run-python runs only what the person allowed", "a scheduled turn never runs Python" and "with Ask me before each snippet runs off"; desktop/oshal-node/plugins/blender/orbit_snippet.py

must_say.fact: viewport-screenshot saves a PNG of the 3D viewport in Orbit's folder and answers in words what it shows: the view, where it looks from, the shading and which objects are in sight. The picture itself does not come back in the answer.
must_say.evidence: scripts/test-blender-plugin-desktop.cjs case "a viewport picture is saved in Orbit's folder and said in words"; crates/oshald/src/computer_apps.rs (an answer carries text, not a picture)

must_say.fact: When Orbit's add-on is not connected in that Blender, Blender cannot be read and the answer says to install it in Orbit Settings, Bound Apps, Install the Blender add-on, then open Blender again.
must_say.evidence: desktop/oshal-node/src/main/bridges/blender.ts NOT_CONNECTED; scripts/test-blender-addon.cjs case "a Blender window without the add-on is refused in words that say where to install it"

must_say.fact: edit-mesh takes operation (extrude, inset, bevel, loop-cut, subdivide, move, scale; never op) and faces: all, selected, a side such as "+z", the face numbers read-object lists, or {"facing": "+x", "near": [x, y, z]} for the one face on that side nearest a point. The new faces become selected, so the next edit can take "selected".
must_say.evidence: scripts/test-blender-game-asset.cjs case "Jarvis's verbs model, unwrap, texture, rig and animate a low-poly character" (a cube box-modelled to 56 vertices, 54 faces, 108 triangles)

must_say.fact: clean-mesh with operation decimate and budget brings a mesh to at most that many triangles; scene-stats counts triangles per object and says whether a budget holds.
must_say.evidence: desktop/oshal-node/scripts/fixtures/blender-game-families.cjs case "the mesh family on a block" (decimated within a budget of 300); scripts/test-blender-game-asset.cjs ("Budget 1000 triangles: within, 892 to spare")

must_say.fact: A game character is made in order: uv-unwrap, texture-material (picture files), add-armature with rig humanoid and fit (Godot's humanoid bone names), skin-to-armature (the answer says how many vertices got weights), then one make-action per animation.
must_say.evidence: scripts/test-blender-game-asset.cjs case "Jarvis's verbs model, unwrap, texture, rig and animate a low-poly character" (21 bones, 56 of 56 vertices weighted, NLA tracks idle and walk)

must_say.fact: export-glb writes each action make-action made as its own animation and says what the .glb holds; Godot's AnimationPlayer then lists them by name.
must_say.evidence: scripts/test-blender-game-asset.cjs case "export-glb puts it in a Godot project, and Godot imports it with idle and walk on its AnimationPlayer" (Godot 4.7.2 --headless --import)

must_say.fact: import-model reads a .glb, .gltf, .fbx or .obj and says what arrived; bake-texture needs UVs and a material and saves a PNG at file, with its res:// path inside a Godot project.
must_say.evidence: desktop/oshal-node/scripts/fixtures/blender-game-families.cjs cases "import-model reads glb, gltf, fbx and obj" and "a chain rig keyed on a pose bone, a shape key, and an ambient-occlusion bake"

must_not_say: A key, a menu path or a mouse step as something Jarvis does: the person's Ctrl+Z and Tab are theirs.
That Jarvis types into, presses or selects anything in Blender.
That run-python is called with confirmed: true before the person said yes in this conversation.
That the viewport picture comes back to Jarvis.
Any declared verb of another program (save-document, insert-paragraph, set-cells and the rest).
Any tool other than computer.app and computer.open.
That run-python runs in a scheduled turn, or without the person's yes while Blender asks before each snippet.
